description: Loui Ridi reached his West Bank home on Monday, more than a week after it came under siege by Israeli settlers — only to find settlers still roaming freely. A Palestinian-American living in Ohio, he traveled to his native village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank to support his brother and nephew, who have been trapped inside the house. The Israeli military declared the area a closed military zone, and Ridi was only able to reach his home under Israeli military escort. CNN’s Jeremy Diamond joined him on the journey.
title: Palestinian-American returns to home under settler siege

In a meeting that lasted more than four hours, US envoy Jared Kushner pressed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to move forward with the Trump-backed Gaza ceasefire plan and “not create obstacles,” according to an Israeli source familiar with the discussions.

Netanyahu, who rejected the 15-point plan earlier this month, said that making progress on the plan was “problematic” because of the upcoming Israeli elections at the end of October, the source told CNN. Courting a right-wing voter base and trailing in repeated polls, Netanyahu has been unwilling to make concessions on Gaza ahead of the elections.

description:
US President Donald Trump threatened today to attack Oman if it interferes with US efforts in the Strait of Hormuz, as the conflict with Iran continues and a two-month window for peace talks expires without a clear path to end the war. 

Trump’s comments come as the 60-day window for peace talks between the US and Iran, agreed to in June, closed Monday without any concrete plans announced for the war to end. Meanwhile, Iran said Monday that its talks with Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz are complex but continuing. 

CNN's Betsy Klein reports from the White House and former George W. Bush aide Michael Allen, CNN political and national security analyst David Sanger and former US Ambassador to the European Union Gordon Sondland break down Trump's harsh rhetoric on Oman.

title: Trump threatens to 'bomb the sh*t' out of Oman

author: CNN
description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that the United States would reduce military exercises with key regional ally South Korea, just hours before they were due to get underway, citing his positive relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Seoul’s lack of assistance with Iran. 

South Korea has been a close American ally for over 70 years and the two nations have a mutual defense treaty, primarily designed to protect it from North Korea –– a burgeoning military power that now possesses nuclear warheads and intercontinental ballistic missiles. 

Retired US Air Force Colonel Cedric Leighton reacts to Trump's move, and former Pentagon official Sabrina Singh explains the significance of the US-South Korea defense alliance. Also, CNN international correspondent Gage Goulding has more details, and former US Ambassador to the European Union Gordan Sondland weighs in on Trump's motives. 

0:00 Military expert speaks out about Trump's decision to scale back joint military exercis
title: 'Unforced error': Military expert on Trump's S Korea decision
